In the Working electrode preparation section, the text states the coated electrodes were “dried at 120 °C for 12 h in vacuum.” The document does not explicitly use the standalone operation term “dry” as the synthesis operation; instead it specifies vacuum drying conditions. Table 2 explicitly lists XRD-derived crystallite sizes for graphite and h-BN before (0 h) and after 2.5 h milling: Lc (nm) = 31 (graphite 0 h), 17 (graphite 2.5 h), 60 (h-BN 0 h), 20 (h-BN 2.5 h); La (nm) = 50 (graphite 0 h), – (graphite 2.5 h, not reported), 155 (h-BN 0 h), 70 (h-BN 2.5 h). These match the extracted values. Figure 1 shows the XRD patterns but does not provide the numeric Lc/La values; the numbers come from Table 2.

Table 2 explicitly lists BET specific surface areas (m2/g) for pristine (0 h) and 2.5 h-milled graphite and h-BN: graphite 9.7 (0 h) and 259.8 (2.5 h); h-BN 1.2 (0 h) and 258.7 (2.5 h). These match the extracted values and units (m2 g-1).

Figure 2 contains SEM images (pristine and 2.5 h-milled h-BN and graphite). The text discussing Fig. 2 states only qualitatively that particle sizes/agglomerates of pristine powders are much larger than milled ones and that the change appears more significant for h-BN, but it does not provide a quantified or explicitly stated “particle size reduction” metric/value. The extracted entry has an empty value/unit, which is not explicitly supported as a stated metric in the paper.
